# Reviewer pack -- SAP control surface, fidelity review

*Generated by `python3 pub/make_r1_pack.py`. Do not edit by hand.*

## What this is, and what is deliberately missing

This is a **specification of a reconstructed SAP control surface**. It is one
part of a larger piece of work, and it is the only part being sent, on purpose.

**The question.** For each mechanism below: *is this a faithful description of
how SAP actually behaves?* Not whether it is a good model, not whether the
omissions matter, not whether you would have modelled it this way. Only whether
what is written is true of the product.

**Why you are not being shown any conclusions.** The rest of the work reaches
findings that depend on some of these descriptions being right. If you could
see which answers help and which hurt, this would stop being a fidelity review
and become a request for agreement. So the findings, the results, the numbers
and the argument have all been removed.

**What would be most useful.** For each mechanism, one of:

- *faithful* -- this is how it behaves;
- *wrong* -- and here is what actually happens;
- *incomplete* -- it behaves this way, and also does X, which is not described;
- *depends* -- it differs by release, deployment model or configuration, in this
  way.

A single line each is worth more than a paragraph. **"Wrong" is the most
valuable answer you can give and the one this pack exists to collect.**

**Scope.** This asks about SAP, not about any deployment of it. Please answer
from product knowledge, not from any organisation's configuration. Nothing here
needs, or should have, anything specific to your employer's systems.

**Product and release.** Deliberately unfixed. If the honest answer to a
question is *that depends on the release*, say so -- that answer is itself among
the most useful this review can produce.

## Evidence levels used below

| level | meaning |
|:---|:---|
| **FORMAL** | a result about the shape of the modelled control |
| **IMPL** | a result in the reference implementation |
| **SAP** | a verified claim about a deployed SAP mechanism, primary-sourced |

None of the mechanisms below has reached the highest evidence level. This review is intended to identify corrections, release dependencies and authoritative sources for the separate primary-source pass; it does not by itself promote a mechanism to that level.

## The one question that matters most

If you answer nothing else: **does any value limit, tolerance or threshold in FI retain state across documents -- a running total, a period accumulation, a per-principal counter -- or is every such limit evaluated against one document at a time?** Both answers are useful and neither is the one being hoped for.
